messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — security just sent a new compliance checklist for telemetry. They want span attribute redaction, envelope encryption for exporters, and stronger audit trails. Can we triage impact? :eyes:

amanda: Ack. Do we have an inventory of which attributes downstream currently contain PII? I know errors and db calls leak params sometimes.

maria: We do — saved a quick list in the audits doc but it's incomplete. Typical culprits: user.email, user.phone, request.query, sql.params, headers.authorization.

kevin: Quick tradeoffs: deterministic hashing of user IDs keeps joinability but is reversible if salt leaked. Full redaction kills traceability (hard to correlate traces). Tokenization with a secure mapping (vault) buys both but adds lookups & latency.

luca: From infra side, envelope encryption on OTLP exporters (client-side) + server-side key rotation looks doable. We should integrate with KMS/HSM. Proposal: split keys per-tenant (or per-org) to limit blast radius.

amanda: For immediate mitigation, security asked for attribute-level redaction rules at collector: drop emails, phones, cc numbers; mask tokens in headers. I sketched an otel-collector processor snippet we could canary: ```processors/transform: - type: attributes - actions: - key: user.email action: delete - key: request.query action: replace - value: "<REDACTED>" - key: headers.authorization action: regexp_replace - pattern: "Bearer\s+\S+" - replace: "Bearer <REDACTED>"```

maria: That looks fine as a stop-gap. Need to log that redaction happened (audit) but not log the original value anywhere. Also retention: security wants raw payloads kept for 7 days encrypted, then fully redacted afterward for standard orgs; extended retention for legal holds only.

kevin: Operational questions: how will redaction interact with routing policies? We have dynamic routing by customer tiers — Dedicated customers may require no redaction (private deployment) vs hosted where redaction applies. Config must be per-deployment/pool.

ops-bot: deploy: otel-collector/transform-v1 -> canary on eng-platform pool at 1769125000 by kevin

luca: Also need to consider metrics/search UX: if we delete user.email we lose ability to filter traces by user. Suggest we create a pseudonym field user.pseudonym that is deterministic-hash(email, tenant_salt) stored instead of plaintext for analytics. Document and encrypt the salt per-tenant.

amanda: Security: deterministic pseudonymization accepted if key material is tenant-scoped and rotated. They require HSM-backed salt storage and an audit trail for all key accesses. We should add a read-only role for the observability team to prevent mass exfil.

maria: Testing checklist for rollout: 1) unit tests for transform rules (regex + edge cases), 2) integration test with downstream storage to ensure indexing doesn't explode, 3) canary on 2% traffic for 48 hours, 4) security-runbook for key compromise, 5) run eval prompts to ensure no visible PII in dashboards.

kevin: Can we measure the perf impact? Tokenization + vault lookups might add ~5–15ms per trace in worst-case. We can batch tokenization or cache mappings but must TTL carefully.

luca: For exporters: prefer OTLP/gRPC with TLS + mTLS between collector and our backend. If customers export to external SaaS, we must support client-side envelope encryption and rotated keys.

amanda: Action items: kevin to roll canary transform today; luca to draft KMS/HSM per-tenant key model; maria to update audit doc and retention policy language; sanjay to coordinate legal sign-off for retention windows.

sanjay: Thanks — aim to have initial canary + metrics by EOD tomorrow. Ping me in thread if anything blocks.
